sleep.wake.label: wake
sleep.wake.title: Inspector Rust keeps the Mac awake — it neither sleeps nor locks. Turn it off with `wakelock off` (or `caffeine off`).
sleep.nosleep.label: no-sleep
sleep.nosleep.title: The power profile is set to `sleep 0` — the Mac never sleeps on its own. This comes from the profile, not the wakelock; reset it with `nosleep off`.
sleep.infinite.label: awake ∞
sleep.infinite.title: The Mac is kept awake with no time limit (an assertion without a timeout).
sleep.timed.label: awake {time}
sleep.timed.title: The Mac is kept awake — this is how long until it may sleep again.
sleep.sleepable.label: sleep
sleep.sleepable.title: Nothing keeps the Mac awake — it may go to sleep.

footer.timers.other: {n} timers running — will fire a notification + sound
footer.tracking.paused_title: Time tracking paused (idle). Type `track off` to stop, or `track` to open the timesheet.
footer.tracking.active_title: Time tracking active. Type `track off` to stop, or `track` to open the timesheet.
footer.darkwake.on_title: Dark Wake on: the system stays awake, the display may sleep — remote connections (SSH/Claude Code) stay reachable. Click turns it off. The lid must stay open.
footer.darkwake.off_title: Turn on Dark Wake: the display may sleep, the system stays awake — remote connections stay reachable (caffeinate -is, no sudo).

set.backup.pw_short: Password must be at least 4 characters.
set.sounds.subtitle: Play short feedback cues for actions: snippet expansion, OCR recognised, screenshot captured, recording start/stop, and copy to clipboard.
set.sounds.on: On — actions play a short sound
set.sounds.dslr: DSLR shutter — mirror slap + double curtain
set.sounds.preview: Picking a style plays it once as a preview. From the procedurally synthesized sound-effects library.
set.gestures.subtitle: Bind trackpad gestures (3–5-finger swipes and taps, tip-taps) to actions: volume, mute, tabs, any key shortcut, an Inspector Rust action, a URL or file, or an AI task — everywhere or per app. Starts with 3-finger swipe up / down → volume and 3-finger tap → mute. Off by default. macOS uses the private MultitouchSupport framework; if gestures don't fire, grant Input Monitoring (System Settings → Privacy & Security).
set.gestures.on: On — gestures run the bindings below
set.gestures.bindings_help: Which gesture does what — freely assignable, takes effect from the next gesture.
set.gestures.typing_guard_help: Ignore gestures for 250 ms after a single keystroke and 600 ms while you type — palms brushing the trackpad while typing are the most common accidental trigger. Applies to every binding with the typing guard on (switch it per binding in the table above). Shortcuts (⌘/⌃ + key) don't count; unmuting is never blocked. Uses the app's keyboard monitor (Accessibility) for the key timing — only when, never which key.
set.gestures.live_help: Type `gestures` in the search bar: live trackpad, thresholds per device, the last decisions, `gestures calibrate` and `gestures record`. Saved recordings are listed and deleted there.
set.snap.title: Window snapping
set.snap.subtitle: Drag a window to a screen edge to snap it: top → maximize, left/right → half. A preview shows the target zone; release to snap. Off by default. Needs Accessibility (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility).
set.snap.on: On — drag a window to an edge to snap it
set.snap.delay_help: The zone preview only appears after the cursor RESTS at the edge this long — placing a window near an edge no longer triggers snapping; pausing there does. Esc still cancels.
set.wrap.subtitle: When the pointer is pushed past an outer edge of your display arrangement, it reappears on the opposite side (Pac-Man wrap) — so you never have to swipe all the way back across a wide or multi-monitor desktop. Inspired by Infinity Monitor. On by default. Needs Accessibility (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility).
set.wrap.on: On — the pointer wraps at the outer edges
set.wrap.deadzone_help: Near a corner the pointer does NOT wrap, so macOS Hot Corners stay reachable.
set.wrap.drag_off: Off — won't wrap while a button is held (won't drop a drag)
set.palette.title: Window palette
set.palette.subtitle: A palette with preset layouts and a hex grid you drag a region over to snap the window there. Off by default. Needs Accessibility (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility).
set.palette.help_titlebar: Hold Control+Option and point at a window's title bar.
set.palette.help_hotkey: Opens for the focused window — bind it under Global shortcuts.
set.palette.help_hidden: Only the Inspector Rust palette appears at the button. Running apps usually follow at once; an app that still shows the macOS menu picks it up after a restart.
set.palette.help_beside: macOS opens its own tiling menu at the button too; the palette places itself beside it, so the two never stack.
set.palette.hide_menu: Hide macOS's tiling menu at the green button
set.palette.shortcut_always: The global shortcut works in every mode.
set.alarm.subtitle: How a finished timer / countdown / alarm alerts you.
set.alarm.overlay_help: (default) — a loud sound (system volume is raised while it rings) + a fullscreen overlay you click to stop.
set.alarm.notification_help: — the classic quiet system notification + a short sound.
set.shortcuts.subtitle: Rebind the global action hotkeys. Press a combo to set it (Backspace clears, Esc cancels); a conflict with any other binding is rejected. Note for Windows: Ctrl+Shift+T is the browser's 'reopen closed tab' — rebind Timesheet here to avoid the clash.
set.expander.subtitle: Type a snippet abbreviation in any text field, then press your hotkey to replace it with the snippet body. Like aText / TextExpander.
set.ax.detected_help: macOS caches the trust check per process, so the running Inspector Rust can't use the just-granted permission until it relaunches. The new instance takes about a second to start.
set.ax.later_title: Dismiss this prompt — the expander will work next time you launch Inspector Rust
set.expander.hotkey_help: Press a key combination, or pick a preset. Backspace clears, Esc cancels. Names match the W3C KeyboardEvent.code spec (Digit1, KeyE, Backquote, …). Tip: digit keys (Alt+1 …) are the most reliable — they're in the same place on every keyboard layout.
set.diag.title: Diagnose expansion (no paste)
set.diag.help: Type a snippet abbreviation in any text field, place the cursor right after it, then click **Diagnose**. Inspector Rust hides its popup, captures the word before your cursor, looks it up — and reports what it found, without pasting. This isolates the lookup from the paste step so you can see exactly where expansion is breaking.
set.diag.fallback: Clipboard fallback — the focused app didn't expose accessibility info
set.diag.no_match: no match — add a snippet with this abbreviation
set.diag.empty_help: An empty capture usually means the popup didn't lose focus fast enough, or there was no text before your cursor. Try again with the cursor placed right after a typed abbreviation.
set.diag.nomatch_help: The capture worked, but no snippet has {abbr} as its abbreviation. Open the **Snippets** tab and create one, or pick a different abbreviation.
set.expander.how1: When you press the hotkey, Inspector Rust synthesizes `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+←` to select the previous word, copies it and looks it up in your snippets.
set.expander.how2: On a hit, the snippet body is written to the clipboard and `Cmd/Ctrl+V` pastes over the still-selected abbreviation.
set.expander.how3: On a miss, the selection stays visible (visual cue) and your clipboard is left untouched.
set.expander.how4: Caveats: **terminals** (iTerm2, Terminal.app, kitty, …) don't expose the input line via accessibility and have no GUI "select previous word" — the abbreviation hotkey does nothing there. Use a **Direct hotkey → snippet** slot (below) or the popup instead. Password fields refuse synthetic paste in many apps.
set.privacy.subtitle: Keep secrets out of the clipboard history, and auto-wipe sensitive copies.
set.privacy.exclude_help: One app name (or part of it) per line or comma-separated — e.g. 1Password, KeePassXC, Bitwarden. Case-insensitive substring match against the frontmost app.
set.privacy.autoclear_help: Wipes a copied value this many seconds later (a newer copy cancels it). 0 = off.
set.ae.title: Auto-expansion (aText style)
set.ae.subtitle: Snippets expand automatically as you type — no hotkey, in any app. Like aText / TextExpander.
set.ae.needs_ax: Passive keyboard monitoring needs macOS Accessibility — grant it in the section above, then the mode switches on.
set.ae.enable_help: Watches your typing system-wide and replaces abbreviations automatically.
set.ae.immediate_help: As soon as the abbreviation is typed
set.ae.undo_help: A Backspace right after the expansion restores the abbreviation.
set.ae.note1: Works in TextEdit/Notepad, Mail, Slack/Discord (Electron), Chrome/Safari/Edge, VS Code and many more.
set.ae.note3: Placeholders such as {date}, {clipboard} and {cursor} work here too.
set.ae.note4: Terminals: limited depending on the OS. Linux (Wayland) offers no system-wide tap — the hotkey/popup route remains there.
set.slots.subtitle: Press a hotkey, paste a snippet's body straight away — no abbreviation typed. Reads nothing, so it works in any app, including terminals (iTerm2, Terminal.app, …).
set.slots.needs_ax: These hotkeys synthesize `Cmd+V`, so they need macOS Accessibility access too — grant it in the section above.
set.slots.empty: No direct slots yet. Add one to bind a hotkey straight to a snippet.
set.slots.help: Pick a hotkey that doesn't clash with your text-expander hotkey, {popup}, or {ocr} — the backend rejects collisions. Long bodies are fine (it pastes, doesn't type). The clipboard is restored afterward.
set.appearance.subtitle: Choose a colour theme. System follows your OS light/dark setting; Light and Dark override it.
set.appearance.follow_os: Following your operating system's light/dark setting.
set.appearance.forced_light: Forced light — ignores the OS setting until you switch back to System.
set.appearance.forced_dark: Forced dark — ignores the OS setting until you switch back to System.
set.appearance.anim_off: All decorative motion is off — the popup appears instantly (countdown rings keep ticking).
set.appearance.anim_reduced: Transitions are instant; the popup power-on is skipped.
set.appearance.anim_full: Full also honours your OS “reduce motion” setting. Applies live, no restart.
set.appearance.size_help: Popup window dimensions — Small 600×430, Medium 700×500, Large 840×600. Applies immediately and recentres on the next open.
set.appearance.lineage_toggle: Connect a copy to the entry it came from
set.appearance.lineage_help: When you copy an entry in another shape (plain text, UPPERCASE, Base64 …), the copy becomes a new entry at the top while the original stays put. Coloured paths on the left of the list tie the two together, like a commit graph. Purely visual — switching this off changes nothing about what gets copied.
set.startup.subtitle_mac: Have Inspector Rust launch automatically when you log in. Uses a LaunchAgent (~/Library/LaunchAgents/InspectorRust.plist) — no Dock icon, opens hidden in the tray.
set.startup.subtitle_win: Have Inspector Rust launch automatically when you sign in. Registered via the Windows run key — opens hidden in the system tray.
set.startup.on: Enabled — Inspector Rust launches on login
set.startup.keepalive_on: On — relaunches within ~30 s if it ever isn't running (crash / quit). Turn off to quit for good.
set.startup.keepalive_off: Off — the app stays closed once you quit it
set.paste.subtitle: Control how clipboard entries land in the destination app.
set.paste.plain_on: HTML / RTF entries are stripped to plain text on paste
set.paste.plain_off: Original formatting is preserved when pasting HTML / RTF
set.paste.tip: hold `Shift` while pressing `Enter` in the popup to paste with original formatting **this once**, regardless of the toggle above.
set.capture.title: Capture
set.capture.subtitle: OCR and screenshot region capture (Ctrl+Shift+O / Ctrl+Shift+S).
set.capture.keep_source: Keep OCR source image in history
set.capture.keep_on: OCR saves both the source PNG and the recognised text to history
set.capture.keep_off: OCR saves only the recognised text — the source PNG is discarded
set.inputlock.subtitle: Type `freeze` in the popup to block all keyboard + mouse input — release with the configured chord.
set.inputlock.chord_help: Click Capture, then press the keys you want to use simultaneously. Release any key to save. Esc cancels.
set.inputlock.safety: OS-level shortcuts ({keys}) always work — Inspector Rust can't intercept them, so you can never be truly locked out. Linux Wayland is not supported by the underlying grab API (X11 sessions only).
set.cheatsheet.title: Keyboard shortcuts
set.cheatsheet.subtitle: Global shortcuts fire from anywhere on your system. Popup shortcuts only fire while Inspector Rust's popup is visible.
set.clean.subtitle: Delete cache / log / temp files inside known-safe folders. Type `clean` in the search bar — it always shows a preview and deletes only after you confirm.
set.clean.aggressive_warn: Aggressive also deletes global dev-tool caches (npm/pnpm/Gradle/Cargo) — they have to be downloaded again afterwards.
set.clean.dev_roots_help: One path per line. Searched for `node_modules` / `target` of projects that haven't been touched for a long time. Empty = no project search.
set.clean.stale: A project counts as dead after
set.clean.stale_help: Days without a change to its manifest, sources or Git HEAD.
set.clean.safety: Only files inside fixed cache / log / temp folders are deleted — never documents, the desktop or the like. Symlinks are never followed. A `node_modules` / `target` is only touched when a `package.json` or `Cargo.toml` really sits next to it. Tools (Docker, Homebrew, pnpm, simctl) are only called when installed — never with sudo.
set.backup.subtitle: Export the whole app — clipboard history, snippets, notes, 2FA accounts and every setting — to a single file, optionally password-encrypted (AES-256-GCM, Argon2id). Import merges: snippets upsert by abbreviation, history dedupes by hash, settings overwrite by key, 2FA/timesheet dedupe; notes append.
set.backup.always: Always: clipboard history (incl. pins & notes) · snippets · notes · 2FA accounts · all settings
set.backup.timesheet: Timesheet data (sessions, events, categories — can be large)
set.backup.no_recovery: There is no recovery — without the password the backup is unreadable.
set.backup.merge_note: Import merges into the current database
set.about.subtitle: Version, license, project info.
set.perm.explainer: **Set up permissions** wipes any stale macOS TCC entry for Inspector Rust (via `tccutil reset`, no admin password) and re-fires the macOS permission prompt. Click **Allow → Open System Settings** and flip the **Inspector Rust** switch — once both grants are in, this card offers a restart. macOS only lets you flip the switch yourself; the reset removes the friction when a switch looks on but Inspector Rust still asks.
set.perm.ax_hint: Lets Inspector Rust paste and run the text expander
set.perm.screen_hint: Lets the OCR and screenshot region capture work
set.perm.finder_hint: Lets Ctrl+Shift+F read the current Finder selection
set.perm.stuck: Switch is already on, but it still doesn't work?
set.perm.stuck_help: macOS keys each grant to the app's code signature. Since v0.23.2 `scripts/install-macos.sh` signs every build with a stable self-signed certificate, so a grant survives rebuilds — this should only be needed once. If a switch shows on but Inspector Rust still asks, the grant is stale: reset it, then re-toggle and relaunch.
set.perm.reset_confirm: Reset the stale Accessibility + Screen Recording + Automation→Finder grants for Inspector Rust and re-fire the macOS prompts? Use this when a switch shows on but Inspector Rust still asks for permission.
set.perm.quit_confirm: Quit Inspector Rust now? Re-launch it via Spotlight / Dock to pick up a freshly granted permission.
set.ts.subtitle: Opt-in time tracking (track on/off). Records app usage by focus; idle auto-pauses; window titles and URLs are encrypted at rest. Nothing leaves your machine (the browser extension uses a loopback socket only).
set.ts.idle_help: Inactivity beyond this retroactively pauses the active interval as idle.
set.ts.retention_help: On the next “track on”, events older than this are deleted. 0 = keep forever.
set.ts.claude_help: Watch ~/.claude/projects for active Claude Code usage per project (time + tokens).
set.ts.goal_help: Target active time per day (0 = off). Shows a progress bar in the Timesheet day view.
set.ts.denylist_help: Comma/newline-separated app names or hostnames. For matches, only the app name + time are stored — no window title or URL.
set.ts.rules_help: Auto-categorize future events. Set rules by assigning a category to an app in the Timesheet's “By app” view; remove them here.
set.pulse.title: Pulse
set.pulse.subtitle: Background monitoring of memory pressure, swap and SSD writes (`pulse` command). Raw samples stay in RAM; one aggregate row a minute goes to a separate pulse.db.
set.pulse.measure_help: Every 5 s system counters, every 30 s the processes. Off → nothing is read or written.
set.pulse.notify: Notify when memory pressure stays red
set.pulse.notify_help: After {n} minutes, naming the biggest consumer — at most once an hour.
set.pulse.tbw_help: TB · empty = automatic (600 TB per TB of capacity). Only used for the forecast.
set.behavior.subtitle: How the main overlay dismisses.
set.behavior.blur_help: Off → the overlay stays open when focus moves elsewhere; close it with `Esc` (an open inline panel consumes the first Esc as “back” — press it twice) or the popup hotkey. Applies immediately, no restart.
set.psi.subtitle: API key for the `pagespeed` command. Without your own key, all users share Google's small daily quota.
set.psi.key_help: Free in the Google Cloud console (PageSpeed Insights API). Stays on this computer; it only leaves it as a parameter of the request to Google.
set.psi.ip_note: ⚠️ A Google key can carry an **IP restriction**. A key bound like that only works from the allowed address — from this computer it then reports “IP address restriction”. The restriction is set in the Google Cloud console.
set.repos.subtitle: Where “Clone” in the `repo` panel puts a GitHub repository, and the access for private repos.
set.repos.dir_help: If a repo's folder is already taken, “name (2)”, “name (3)” … is created — nothing is overwritten.
set.repos.gh_help: `gh` is installed — if it is logged in (`gh auth login`), its token is used. A token here is the fallback.
set.repos.token_help: For private repos. Kept in the keychain, only sent to github.com and never put on a command line.
set.active_help: Off = no background thread, no file access.
set.gh.subtitle: Statistics of your GitHub account for the `github` command. Read-only; the history stays local in history.db.
set.gh.connect_help: Opens github.com in the browser and asks for a code — no password goes through Inspector.
set.gh.no_client: Browser sign-in isn't set up in this build — use a token under “Advanced” or `gh auth login`.
set.gh.auto_help: At start and then at most once per interval; never faster than the rate limit allows.
set.gh.private_help: OAuth apps have no read-only access to private repos — so the sign-in asks for `repo` (read AND write; Inspector never writes). More frugal: a fine-grained token with “Metadata: read” under “Advanced”. Takes effect at the next sign-in.
set.gh.pat_help: Fallback if you don't want to sign in in the browser. Kept in the keychain (shared with the `repo` command) and never shown.
set.ds.subtitle: The same data on several Macs — through a shared folder (e.g. iCloud Drive). Off by default.
set.ds.folder_help: Must be the same synced folder on every device.
set.ds.pass_help: Encrypts the stored files. Enter the same one on EVERY device; it only lives in the keychain and is never synced.
set.ds.totp_help: Off. Only turn it on if you are aware that the codes then sit in the shared folder (encrypted).
set.ds.no_deletes: Deletions are deliberately NOT transferred: the devices merge their data. An empty state can therefore never overwrite a full one.
set.ab.replace_confirm: Replace everything: the current state is replaced by this backup. Anything added since the backup is lost. Continue?
set.ab.subtitle: Backs up settings, snippets, notes, 2FA (and optionally the history) at a fixed interval to a folder of your choice — e.g. a Google Drive or iCloud folder, optionally encrypted. Off by default.
set.ab.folder_help: An existing folder, e.g. your synced Google Drive or iCloud folder.
set.ab.interval_help: How often to check. Only written when something changed.
set.ab.keep_help: Older backups are deleted automatically (only our own files).
set.ab.encrypt_help: Recommended for cloud folders. AES-256, the password lives only in the keychain.
set.ab.password_help: ⚠️ Without this password the backup is worthless — also note it in a password manager. It is never stored in a file.
set.ab.history_help: Off = smaller files (the history with images is what makes them big). Settings, snippets, notes and 2FA are always included.
set.ab.timesheet_help: Off. Timesheet data is often large and bound to this device.
set.ab.totp_warn: ⚠️ 2FA secrets are backed up too. Without encryption they sit in plain text in this folder — for a cloud folder you should turn encryption on.
set.ab.merge_help: Merge only adds (never deletes). “Replace everything” restores exactly this state — anything later is lost.
set.ab.none_found: No backups found in the folder.
set.sync.subtitle: Syncs snippets automatically with cue (cue.celox.io) — both ways, including deletions. Which groups take part is switched in cue with the ☁️ icon in the group header; on conflicts the higher version wins (cue on a tie).
set.sync.enable_help: — every 60 s and after every snippet change
set.sync.token_help: Generate it in cue under Settings → Snippet sync (Inspector Rust) and paste it here.
set.keys.ocr_hint: Drag a marquee over text on screen → text → clipboard
set.keys.shot_hint: Drag a marquee → PNG → clipboard + history (no OCR)
set.keys.color_hint: Click a pixel → hex (#RRGGBB) → clipboard + history
set.keys.paste_hint: Plain-text downgrade follows the Paste setting
set.keys.paste_fmt_hint: One-shot override of the plain-text setting
set.keys.save_image_hint: Saves the entry's PNG bytes unchanged
set.keys.transform_hint: On a selected text entry — see the preview toolbar
set.popup_hk.subtitle: The global shortcut that opens the search popup. Change it if the default collides with another app you use.
set.popup_hk.help: Press a key combination, or pick a preset. Backspace clears, Esc cancels. {modifier} alone isn't supported by the global-shortcut plugin — pick a combo with at least one regular key (Cmd+Space, Cmd+J, …).
set.history_hk.subtitle: A second, optional global shortcut that also opens the clipboard history — alongside the main popup hotkey. Clear it to disable.
set.history_hk.help: Press a key combination, or pick a preset. Backspace / the Disable button clears it (turns the second hotkey off).
set.bruno.title: Bruno — gross/net defaults
set.bruno.subtitle: These values apply to every `bruno <€>` call. Tax year 2025 (simplified; not tax advice).
set.bruno.state_help: Affects the church-tax rate (BW + BY: 8 %, otherwise 9 %).
set.bruno.children_help: Affects long-term care insurance (reduction from child #2) and the child allowance.
set.bruno.church_yes: Yes, member of a church-tax-collecting religious community
set.bruno.health_add_help: The health insurer's additional contribution. Average 2025 ≈ 2.5 %. TK: 2.45 %, Barmer: 3.29 %.
set.bruno.business_help: Freelancers (§ 18 EStG) pay no trade tax; trades (§ 15) with a €24,500 allowance + § 35 credit.
set.bruno.hebesatz_help: Your municipality's multiplier (e.g. Berlin 410, Munich 490, national average ≈ 400).
set.bruno.kv_help: Voluntary statutory insurance (GKV) is calculated on the profit (minimum/maximum assessment base); private insurance (PKV) as a fixed monthly premium incl. private long-term care.
set.bruno.sickpay_help: With sick pay: general rate 14.6 %; without: reduced 14.0 % (+ the additional rate above).
set.bruno.pkv_amount_help: Full monthly premium incl. private long-term care insurance.
set.bruno.joint_help: Married + joint assessment → splitting tariff instead of the basic tariff.
set.faker.title: Faker — fake-data defaults
set.faker.subtitle: Applied to every `faker` call and `{faker:…}` snippet placeholder.
set.faker.locale_help: Used when a generator isn't given an @locale. Many generators fall back to English where a locale has no data.
set.faker.count_help: How many values `faker <gen>` produces when no count is typed (1–10000).
set.faker.pinned_help: Comma-separated generator names to float to the top of the `faker` catalogue (e.g. person, email, uuid).
set.faker.history_help: When on, generated data is also stored as a clipboard-history entry. Turn off so bulk test data doesn't flood the history.
set.faker.history_toggle: Store faker output in clipboard history
set.figlet.title: Figlet — ASCII-art banner defaults
set.figlet.subtitle: Applied to every `figlet` command; the option chips still override per banner.
set.figlet.font_help: The font a bare `figlet <text>` starts with (browse/override with @font).
set.figlet.width_help: Wrap width in columns (0 = no wrapping).
set.figlet.comment_help: Wrap the banner as a source comment by default (for banner headers in code).
set.figlet.trim_help: Remove trailing spaces from each line (clean paste into code). Internal alignment is preserved.
set.figlet.box_toggle: Draw a box around the banner
set.figlet.pinned_help: Comma-separated font names to float to the top of the gallery (e.g. standard, slant, doom).
set.figlet.history_help: When on, a copied banner is also stored as a clipboard-history entry.
set.figlet.history_toggle: Store figlet banners in clipboard history
set.sec.subtitle: Defaults for the sec / nmap / sqlmap / ferox / john command builders. Authorized targets only — Inspector Rust builds commands, it never scans.
set.sec.scope_help: Shown in the preview header — your reminder of the engagement you're authorized for.
set.sec.wordlist_help: Used by feroxbuster / John when you don't type one. Pick a common path or type your own.
set.sec.path_missing: Path not found on this machine
set.sec.timing_help: Left empty = not injected. Timing 0–5 (nmap -T), threads (ferox -t), rate (ferox --rate-limit).

banner.paste_ax: **Paste failed — macOS Accessibility access not granted.** Open the **Settings** tab and click **Force re-grant** in the amber banner. After granting in System Settings, click **Restart now**.
banner.ocr: **OCR failed — macOS Screen Recording access not granted.** Without it, `screencapture` is denied and the region marquee never appears. Grant it in **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording** for Inspector Rust, then relaunch.
banner.expander_ax: **Text expansion failed — macOS Accessibility access not granted.** Inspector Rust can't read the focused field or type the snippet without it. Use **Force re-grant** in the amber banner below, then click **Restart now**.
banner.finder: **Finder selection unavailable — macOS Automation access not granted.** Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation → Inspector Rust** and turn **Finder** on. Then press **Ctrl+Shift+F** again.
banner.expander_password: **Text expansion blocked — the focused field is a password input.** Refused on purpose: pasting a snippet into a credential field would leak the body into your password manager / sudo prompt / OS password dialog.
banner.expander_secure: **Text expansion blocked — secure event input is active.** macOS is suppressing synthetic input (typically because a password field has keyboard focus). Try again after leaving the secure field.
banner.expander_empty: **Nothing to expand — no freshly typed abbreviation.** In terminals the expander works from the keys you **just typed** (it can't read the input line); a click, arrow key, Enter or Esc right before the hotkey clears that buffer. Type the abbreviation and press the hotkey immediately — or **type it here in the search bar** and press **⏎** to paste, or use a **Direct hotkey → snippet** (Settings).
banner.expander_nomatch: **What you just typed matches no snippet abbreviation.** In terminals the expander works from the keys you just typed — the last word didn't match any abbreviation (check the exact spelling in the Snippets tab). about.tagline: Clipboard productivity toolkit for power users — searchable history, snippets with auto-expansion, calculator, colour picker + eyedropper, image tools, OCR + screenshots (capture modes, annotate, pin), cleaning, and monitor brightness.
about.workflow: One hotkey, no mouse. Search the clipboard history, expand snippets system-wide (passive auto-expansion or a hotkey), calculate inline, sample colours, recolour and cut out images, capture & annotate screenshots, free up disk space, dim your monitors — without leaving the keyboard. Local SQLite, AES-256 encrypted at rest, no telemetry, no cloud.

The download then fetches ONLY the section (yt-dlp --download-sections, frame-accurate) — 20 s out of an 83-minute set arrive as ~1.2 MiB. Collapsed = the download is byte-identical to before.

fx.link_grabber.note: Paste anything — a list, a chat log, an e-mail — and every YouTube / Instagram / TikTok / Facebook / Dailymotion link in it is picked out, deduplicated and downloaded one after another. A failing link is recorded on its row and the queue continues; Retry re-runs only the failures. Audio is offered when every link is YouTube. The popup stays pinned for the run and Finder opens once at the end, not once per file. Each row shows a small thumbnail, the title, channel and duration before anything is downloaded — cached per URL, debounced, at most three lookups at once (each costs ~4 s).
